typescript.x-note: Design 1, rejected: keep the regex on the whole .execute argument text and skip ${} spans first. A regex cannot see nested substitutions, quotes, and inner templates, and it would treat a plain template the same as a sql tag, so db.execute(`SELECT ${"d2d-canonical:" + id}`) would pass even though JavaScript splices that value into the statement. Design 2, used: a + beside a quote matches only on a binary_expression that is not inside a template_substitution of a call whose callee is sql or ends in .sql. Drizzle binds that interpolation as a parameter (sql`... ${"d2d-canonical:" + id} ...`). The same + in a string or a plain template passed to .execute stays a finding. Any sql.raw( call stays a finding, including a constant or a sanitized argument, because the tree does not show that the text is static. A tag whose callee is not named sql is not this exemption.

feedback.message: {symbol} concatenates a value into SQL or passes it through sql.raw. Use the query builder or a parameterized sql`` template.
